ai.title: CLI 1.0.616 release ships with new models, stream fixes, and table
ai.summary: This release bundles several user-visible improvements across the CLI and agent runtime, including new model support for claude-opus-4.6, kimi-k2.5, and glm-4.7, fixes for Anthropic tool call ordering and orphaned tool call filtering on abort, and word-wrapping for markdown table cells in the terminal renderer. The SDK 0.10.5 addresses missing tool calls, and Claude subscription support now shows deprecation warnings directing users to migrate via /subscribe. These changes span cli/, packages/agent-runtime/, sdk/, common/, and web/ packages.
ai.evidence: Version bump in cli/release/package.json changes the "version" field from 1.0.615 to 1.0.616, a one-line change in the release manifest.

eli5.text: This release adds support for three new AI models - Claude Opus 4.6, Kimi K2.5, and GLM-4.7 - so you can now choose more powerful options for your coding tasks. Tables in the terminal now wrap long text across multiple lines instead of cutting it off with ellipsis, making it much easier to read detailed output without losing information. The tool calling system has been fixed so AI assistant function calls and their results always appear in the correct order, preventing errors where results show up without their matching calls. Users with Claude subscriptions will see clear deprecation notices guiding them toward the new Codebuff Strong subscription plan, including FAQ updates about the removal timeline. Aborting interrupted AI responses no longer leaves broken tool call entries that cause provider errors. Upgrading gives you more model choices, cleaner table displays, more reliable tool execution, and clearer guidance if you're transitioning from the old Claude subscription service.

ai.title: Update docs to Claude Opus 4.6
ai.summary: Documentation updates replace references to Claude Opus 4.5 with Claude Opus 4.6 across multiple pages. The changes affect the FAQ, model breakdown, and mode comparison tables to align with the new orchestrator and subagent models. Additionally, markdown table formatting is adjusted for consistency.

eli5.text: If you read Codebuff's documentation today, you'll see updated references to a newer version of its main AI model, replacing the previous version name everywhere the docs mentioned a specific model. The FAQ, model list, and feature comparison pages now describe how the assistant picks different AI systems for different jobs (like code editing vs. research). You'd notice the text mentions a newer model name where it used to say an older one, but the list of which AI handles which task stays the same. The change is live in the published documentation right now.

ai.title: CLI suggestion menu uses per-item same-line layout check
ai.summary: SuggestionMenu now checks if each item's description fits on the same line individually, replacing the previous all-or-nothing menu-wide check. This change calculates available width by subtracting button padding and compares it against maxLabelLength plus item description length. Affects cli/src/components/suggestion-menu.tsx. Mixed-length items no longer force two-line layout for all items if one is too long.

eli5.text: When you type a command and a list of suggestions pops up, each suggestion now decides for itself whether its hint text sits on the same line as the command name or wraps to the next line. Previously, the menu looked at every suggestion at once: if even one hint was too long, every suggestion got pushed onto two lines. Now each suggestion fits as tightly as possible, so short commands with short hints no longer waste vertical space just because another, longer command is in the list.

ai.title: Continue turn when agent emits only think tags
ai.summary: Added logic in `run-agent-step.ts` to detect responses containing only `<think>` tags and no other content. If such a response is received without tool calls, the agent now continues the turn instead of ending it. This prevents premature termination when the model outputs only internal reasoning. The change applies to the core agent runtime loop.

eli5.text: When the assistant is deep in thought and its reply comes back containing nothing but its internal reasoning, it now keeps thinking and continues its turn instead of stopping. This affects the assistant's runtime behavior so that moments of silent, reasoning-only processing no longer cut a turn short, letting the assistant reach a more complete response before handing control back. The behavior is live today.

ai.title: Skill tool prompt forbids phantom skills
ai.summary: Skill tool description and empty-state handling in `common/src/tools/params/tool/skill.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/prompts.ts` now explicitly instruct the model not to call unavailable skills. Previously, the `AVAILABLE_SKILLS_PLACEHOLDER` was silently removed when no skills were registered, allowing the model to hallucinate tool calls for non-existent skills. The update replaces the placeholder with 'There are no skills available. Do not use this tool because there are no skills to load.' and adds a guard clause to the base description. Also removed hardcoded agent name 'Buffy' from tool list header.

eli5.text: You might have noticed the assistant occasionally tried to use skills that didn't exist, as if pretending they were there. Now, when no skills are available, it explicitly says there are none and won't try to use any, stopping these fake attempts. This affects anyone relying on the system's tool usage behavior. The change went live today.

ai.title: Add systeminformation dependency to CLI
ai.summary: Added systeminformation ^5.30.7 to cli/package.json dependencies. Enables OS and hardware metric collection within the CLI runtime. Scope limited to the CLI package manifest.

eli5.text: The CLI now has a new tool built in that lets it look at your computer's operating system and hardware details (like CPU, memory, and disk usage) while it's running. If you were to watch the CLI gather system stats, you'd see it actually pull information from your machine rather than leaving that empty. This only affects the CLI runtime; the change is in place and ready to use today.

ai.title: Revert CLI suggestion menu layout tweak
ai.summary: Reverts `cli/src/components/suggestion-menu.tsx` layout tweak. Restores per-item `itemFitsOnSameLine` check using `availableWidth` instead of global `useSameLine` based on `maxDescriptionLength`. Fixes alignment issues in CLI suggestion menu.

eli5.text: When you type a command and the assistant shows you a list of suggested next steps, each suggestion used to decide on its own whether its hint text could sit on the same line as its label. That quick decision depended on how much total width the whole menu had, without thinking about how long each particular label was. Now, the whole menu looks at every label and hint together and decides in one go whether all hints can sit aligned on the same line, so the layout switches smoothly from stacked to side-by-side instead of some hints jumping to a new line while others stay put. You would see the suggestion menu line up its descriptions more reliably, without the crooked wrapping that happened before.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.617 ships Claude Opus 4.6 docs, think-tag turn fix
ai.summary: Release 1.0.617 bundles documentation updates replacing Claude Opus 4.5 references with Claude Opus 4.6 across the FAQ, model breakdown, and mode comparison tables. The core agent runtime loop in packages/agent-runtime now continues the turn when a response contains only think tags without tool calls, preventing premature termination from internal reasoning output. The skill tool in common and agent-runtime prompts now explicitly forbids calling unavailable skills via an empty-state guard, and the CLI adds systeminformation ^5.30.7 for OS and hardware metric collection.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunk changes version field from 1.0.616 to 1.0.617. Release 1.0.617 bundles prior commits: Claude Opus 4.6 documentation, CLI suggestion menu per-item same-line layout, agent turn continuation for think-tag-only responses, skill tool phantom-skill guard, systeminformation ^5.30.7 dependency, and reverted suggestion menu layout tweak.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.617 brings documentation updates for the new Claude Opus 4.6 model and fixes a problem where the AI would stop talking in the middle of a conversation just because it only showed hidden internal reasoning. The release also improves the command-line suggestion menu so that long and short options display more cleanly together, adds a new safety guard so the AI no longer invents tools that don't exist, and includes a small technical dependency to help gather system information for diagnostics. Upgrading gives you more accurate help docs, smoother on-screen menus, and a more reliable AI that keeps working instead of cutting itself off early.
